sections.heading: Open Spec PRs and Prioritization
sections.summary: 13 PRs are open against EIP-8141; none urgent, but Nethermind flagged a keystore-access PR for ERC 8403 / EIP-8130 compatibility.
sections.body:
- 13 PRs are currently open against the [EIP-8141 spec on forkcast](https://forkcast.org/eips/8141/?tab=history); all are considered secondary to getting Frames DevNet 0 running.
- Daniil (Nethermind) flagged one PR as worth earlier attention: enabling frames to read the key store for compatibility with ERC 8403 and EIP-8130.
  - Marc suggested opening a thread in the frames R&D channel for further discussion.
- lightclient noted he reviewed Ivan's execution-APIs PR for `eth_simulateFrameTx` but disagrees with the approach; prefers extending `simulateV1` into a `simulateV2` that adds frame modes and multidimensional gas info rather than taking the frame tx RLP directly.

sections.heading: Ethrex Testnet Status
sections.summary: The Ethrex-hosted frames testnet has been live 14 days with Ethrex, Geth, and Nethermind validating; nearly 400 frame transactions sent.
sections.body:
- Ivan (ethrex) could not attend but left a written update, relayed by marc: the testnet has been live for 14 days, with three client implementations validating — ethrex, Geth, and Nethermind.
- Nearly 400 frame transactions sent from approximately 21 distinct senders, plus some initiatives to improve tooling.
- Besu (Justin Florentine) has not yet joined; asked what minimum criteria (hive tests, kurtosis configs, EELS) should be met so joining doesn't break the network.
  - Daniil said the only requirement is passing the latest EELS test release; Besu should contact Ivan for the connection details.
- Nethermind noted their mempool verification gas limit is set to 300K (vs. the default 100K) to let more complex frame transactions into blocks; this is a mempool-level difference, not a consensus issue.
- Justin referenced the [execution-specs 8141 branch](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/tree/eips/amsterdam/eip-8141) as the target spec; Spencer noted there should also be a frames-devnet-0 branch.
- Spencer confirmed the [tests-frames-devnet@v0.3.0 release](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/releases/tag/tests-frames-devnet@v0.3.0) is the latest test release, and that the plan is to launch the devnet once clients pass it.

sections.heading: Frames DevNet 0 Launch Timeline
sections.summary: Frames DevNet 0 via PandaOps is blocked on scheduling; Geth, Ethrex, and Nethermind are ready, and marc will follow up with PandaOps.
sections.body:
- Frames DevNet 0 (PandaOps-hosted) has not launched; primary blocker is availability of PandaOps staff who have been out of office.
- lightclient confirmed he is waiting for PandaOps availability.
- At least Geth, Ethrex, and Nethermind are ready to participate.
- Marc committed to following up with PandaOps immediately after the call and communicating a target date in the R&D channel.
- Spencer noted Guru has been the one working on frames testing on the EF side and is out of office until October 5; Spencer plans to pick up where he left off in the interim.

sections.heading: Unified Max Fee and Multidimensional Fee-Market for Frames
sections.summary: Anders presented three proposals — unified max fee, byte-denominated state limits, and EVM gas accounting options — to align frames with a future multidimensional fee-market.
sections.body:
- Anders Elowsson presented ideas from his [Eth Magicians comment](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8141-frame-transaction/27617/172) on harmonizing frame transactions with a future multidimensional fee-market.
- **Unified max fee (EIP-7999 concept):** Replace separate `max_fee_per_gas` and `max_fee_per_blob_gas` with a single fungible `max_fee` across all resources.
  - Prevents transaction failure when one resource's base fee spikes even though the user is willing to pay enough overall.
  - Priority fee would remain per-gas to link tips to actual consumption.
  - Chris (Base) expressed interest: L2s already have a hidden multidimensional fee (L1 data fee) with no user-specified limit; a unified max fee would help.
  - Justin Florentine asked how the max fee interacts with mempool filtering rules — whether transactions whose max fee goes stale as prices fluctuate are held, suspended, or evicted. Anders said the unified max fee is a net benefit here because it absorbs drift between resource prices, so fewer transactions need filtering out.
  - Maria Silva confirmed that max fee validation requires no additional state access beyond what the transaction envelope already contains.
  - lightclient expressed general support but noted concern about unexpected edge cases; will discuss further when he has voice.
- **Byte-denominated state limits:** Express state limits in bytes rather than gas units.
  - Protects users across fork boundaries when cost-per-state-byte is repriced.
  - Wallets would not need to query the gas price to express the limit.
  - More compact encoding and a natural unit of account; can be converted to gas internally upon processing.
- **EVM gas accounting designs:** Six design combinations under consideration (three base designs × with/without universal overflow channel).
  - Aggregate EVM gas: single limit funded at the highest base fee — simple but overfunds.
  - Sub-fee accounting: floating gas prices converted at relative base fee — avoids overfunding but introduces floating prices for developers.
  - Full multidimensional: separate limits per resource — most expressive but complicates legacy call operations.
  - Universal overflow channel: a separate gas budget that any resource can draw from when its own budget is exhausted; legacy `CALL` gas parameter maps to the overflow.
  - Frames already have a frame-level state-gas pool that is not forwarded into subcalls, which partially addresses reservation problems but raises questions about interaction with the overflow design.
- Asked (by Spencer, in chat) how multidimensional fees interact with EIP-8037 on frames vs. other transaction types, Anders said most designs under consideration would remove the 8037 reservoir, though this is not yet precisely specified. Maria Silva countered in chat that the reservoir would still be needed for legacy transactions that don't have separate gas limits; Anders called it a reasonable comment and left it open.
- Spencer asked whether multidimensional fees will be proposed for the I* upgrade; Maria confirmed that is the plan.
- Maria also recommended involving the developers who worked on EIP-8037 gas accounting in the frames gas-accounting discussion.
- Discussion to continue on the [EIP-8141 Eth Magicians thread](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8141-frame-transaction/27617/172).

sections.heading: Viem Implementation Feedback and JSON RPC Gaps
sections.summary: Viem's maintainer reported that JSON RPC support for frame transactions is underspecified; gas estimation and simulation APIs need attention.
sections.body:
- jxom (Viem maintainer) submitted [feedback on the agenda issue](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2221#issuecomment-5770817575) noting friction in implementing frame transaction support.
- Key gaps identified:
  - `eth_estimateGas` or equivalent support for frame gas estimation.
  - `eth_fillTransaction` support.
  - Simulation support via `eth_simulateV1` or a new endpoint.
- Ivan's proposal for a dedicated [`eth_simulateFrameTransaction` endpoint](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/894/changes) was shared; lightclient prefers extending `simulateV1` into a `simulateV2` instead.
- No immediate resolution; discussion to continue async.

sections.heading: EIP-8130 and EIP-8141 Harmonization Effort
sections.summary: Ethlabs presented a comprehensive standard-building effort to implement EIP-8130 on top of EIP-8141 with tooling, clear signing, privacy, and wallet API integration.
sections.body:
- Mislav (Ethlabs) presented an in-progress effort to build a common smart-account standard on top of EIP-8130 and EIP-8141, targeting wallet developers, neobanks, and fintech apps.
- Core goals:
  - Full compatibility with EIP-8130 built on EIP-8141 for Ethereum mainnet.
  - Integration of EIP-7906, EIP-7715, and EIP-7710 (adapted to work with 8130's sessions system; Solidity implementation tested).
  - Exploration of extending ERC-5792 (wallet call API) to support batch expressiveness; if infeasible, a new wallet call API standard will be proposed.
  - Clear signing support, especially for hardware wallets, enabling static reasoning about transaction outcomes via EIP-7902 assertions.
  - Privacy features leveraging capabilities already in EIP-8130.
- Stretch goals (open to discussion/dropping):
  - Smart batching: piping outputs of one batch step into inputs of the next (e.g., unknown slippage in swaps).
  - Cross-chain transactions: single signed payload executing across multiple chains.
  - Compatibility considerations for ERC-4337 and EIP-7702.
- Deliverables will include a mock UI demo showing hardware wallet + software wallet + app interaction with frame transactions.
- Daniil asked about [ERC 8403](https://github.com/ethereum/ERCs/pull/1979) for key management; Mislav acknowledged he missed the earlier discussion but plans to include it, noting the tree-structure approach could work well for cross-L2 key-store configuration via canonical bridges.
  - Daniil requested feedback on whether ERC 8403 works for Ethlabs' system.
- The effort will be formalized as an ERC; initial discussion channels will include an Eth Magicians post and a Telegram group, with more formal channels later.
- Mislav noted that downstream adoption work will take at least a year to get through stakeholder gates.

sections.heading: DevNet Max Verification Gas Limit
sections.summary: Agreement to raise the max verification gas limit above 100K (possibly to 500K) for the frames devnet to enable testing complex scenarios.
sections.body:
- Daniil (Nethermind) proposed raising the max verification gas from the current 100K default to 500K for the devnet to allow testing of more complex frame transaction scenarios.
- lightclient confirmed via chat: "that's fine to me."
- Final parameter to be confirmed async when coordinating with PandaOps on devnet setup.
